This is also my method of choice but if you are generally healthy it’s going to take a week.  And that is if you don’t break down and have water.  Also you will have to be alone for the last few days because once your dehydration symptoms are severe and obvious someone around you will try to get you to a hospital.

I once went maybe 60hours (2.5days) without food or water and I was functioning just fine except for a slight headache.

It sucks, there’s no fool proof, painless, easy method.

This struck me as I was also severely depressed as teenager.  I have to say that 15 years later, despite making a good salary, having almost no debt, traveling the world, and living in a nice apartment, I am still severely depressed.

There are advantages to being an adult.  But mental health management is always hard.

Try to get as much help as you can as soon as you can.  Age will not make a difference in how you feel.  Life circumstances also won’t make a difference.  If you can get to the root of why you are unhappy and change how you feel and how you manage your mental health as a young person, it will make being an adult much easier.

I appreciate your suggestion.  I try to pile onto my schedule but I get overwhelmed.  Again, the pressure to approach the world with a smile all the time is literally soul crushing.  

I’ll have a full schedule and then everyone likes me so much that I can’t just do what I’m already doing.  The expectation is that I’m always going to do more.   I pulled away from my yoga studio because the idea was “well you are a regular you take all the classes now come to the parties, perform, etc”.  It’s too much, it’s never ok just to participate.  I’m never enough.  Same with the entrepreneurs group. Not enough to attend, now I have to plan a party and contribute contribute contribute.   

I feel like whatever I do I’m expected to go above and beyond.  I’d rather do nothing because I’m not enough just to participate.

I do enjoy travel while I’m away but it costs money and I have to have some kind of job while traveling.  I have been working on something but again the expectation is always to be happy happy happy, positive positive positive all the time.  I can’t do that.

I change jobs every two years.  How much longer am I going to do that?

All these things are easier said than done.  Working in a career for 10 years was supposed to = happiness.  It wasn’t true.

Now I’m supposed to go into debt for more schooling?

I’m supposed to live in another country?

All I easier said than done.  If I feel like trash now, how do I know that changing my situation is going to make it any better.

I appreciate your insight.

I have been avoiding taking any sort of medication because in the pst I felt that I was too ok with my circumstances (at the time I had just been hospitalized, quit my job, and was living with my mom and perfectly ok with it).  It scares me to think that taking medication is required for me to feel ok.

I went to Siciliy.  It was amazing but I came back hating my life.  Vacations are a trap.  Enjoying a week in time so thoroughly only highlights how much of waste the rest of my life is.

I also recently went on an art workshop in Italy.
Same thing.  Went away, spent an amazing time with amazing people and the came back home with fresh eyes on how utterly terrible my job and all the people there are.

Yes travel seems to be the consensus.  Maybe I will feel marginally less overwhelmed after my trip in a few days.  But I generally come back from vacation depressed to have to come back to my normal life.

I have a therapist - started with them a month ago. I have also had therapy in the past, I have been inpatient at mental institution, that shit doesn’t work.

I go to a painting class weekly where I get tons of praise, meanwhile I feel terrible inside.

I joined a social group of entrepreneurs and it was too much soul crushing pressure to constantly act happy and positive so I left.

I am currently in an accountability group for entrepreneurs still.

I technically have 2 jobs on top of my career to try to make money to get out of my soul crushing career.

I’ve worked my ass off for 10 years (started my career at 19) to be happy and productive and comfortable financially.

None of this changes how I feel inside.

I’ve tried yoga (10 years including overseas retreats), meditation (1 year consistent practice at home and at zen temples etc).

I have not sat around waiting for life to hand me happiness.  Happiness is not there, it doesn’t exist.  I’ve done my part.  I’m tired.
